mechanism_narrative: A quarterly decline in real GDP (GDPC1) relative to the prior quarter indicates economic contraction, which triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate earnings expectations and heightened risk aversion.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when GDPC1 declines from prior quarter, or Rank IC over entire sample period remains < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points from the prior month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to reduced consumer spending and corporate profit margin pressures.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp from prior month, or Rank IC over entire sample period < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) from the prior month indicates broad-based economic contraction in manufacturing and construction sectors, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to elevated recession risk and equity market volatility.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and HOUST both decline from prior month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO and HOUST both decline from prior month, or Rank IC for interaction signal < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), a decline in real consumer spending (RSAFS) from the prior month signals reduced household purchasing power, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to lower corporate revenue growth expectations.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and RSAFS declines from prior month, or Rank IC for interaction in tightening cycle < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in CPI (CPIAUCSL) from the prior month signals rising inflation, which triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to expectations of monetary policy tightening and higher equity discount rates.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises from prior month, or Rank IC over entire sample period < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly housing starts (HOUST) level falling below 1000 thousand units signals a significant slowdown in residential construction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to reduced consumer confidence and construction sector economic activity.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when HOUST < 1000, or Rank IC over entire sample period < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) from the prior month indicates labor market deterioration, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings growth.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises from prior month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises from prior month, or Rank IC for interaction signal < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 2.5%), a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) from the prior month signals manufacturing contraction, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced economic activity and equity market volatility.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 2.5% and INDPRO declines from prior month, or Rank IC for interaction in tightening cycle < 0.03.
